Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: Acute onset diarrhoea, vomiting, subjective fever, abdominal cramps; brother with identical illness suggests contagious gastroenteritis. Unable to retain oral intake; still passing urine (last 1 h ago) indicating some hydration. No red-flag features of bleeding or severe abdominal localization.

Consistent differential diagnoses (DDx):
• Acute viral gastroenteritis (likely norovirus) – High likelihood: household cluster, sudden onset, watery stool, vomiting.  
• Acute bacterial gastroenteritis/food-borne infection – Moderate likelihood: persisting >72 h, subjective high fever; stool culture arranged.

Working diagnosis: Infectious gastroenteritis (prob. viral vs bacterial).  
Priorities: Prevent dehydration, obtain stool specimen, monitor for deterioration, arrange face-to-face clinical review.

Management Plan

- Continue ORS; advise tiny frequent sips to improve tolerance.  
- Dietary advice: bland foods (toast, biscuits); avoid fruit, vegetables, dairy until recovery.  
- Arrange urgent clinic appointment today for physical assessment (vitals, hydration status) and immediate stool sample submission.  
- Safety-net: attend ED/A&E if worsening symptoms, inability to pass urine, persistent vomiting, or signs of severe dehydration.  
- No empirical antibiotics at this stage; await stool culture results.  
- Patient instructed to phone support line to confirm appointment; clinician to flag as urgent.

Consider:

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.  
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Acute viral gastroenteritis (likely norovirus) – High: rapid family spread, watery diarrhoea, vomiting, usually self-limiting.  
2. Acute bacterial gastroenteritis (Campylobacter/Salmonella/E. coli) – Moderate: fever and persistence >72 h warrant stool culture.
